prompt: Build a least-recently-USED cache on top of LinkedHashMap in access order, so reading a key protects it from eviction. Complete the stubs, then run the tests.
explanation: new LinkedHashMap<>(16, 0.75f, true) switches the map from insertion order to access order, so every successful get or put moves that key to the end of the iteration order. Eviction then only has to drop the FIRST key the iterator yields, which is by definition the least recently used one. Returning entries.get(key) directly is enough for get, because the map reorders itself on a hit and leaves itself alone on a miss.
hints: The third constructor argument of LinkedHashMap is accessOrder -- pass true to get least-recently-used ordering.
After put, if size() > capacity, take entries.keySet().iterator(), call next() once, then remove() to drop the oldest entry.
Once the map is in access order, get can just delegate to entries.get(key) and keysOldestFirst is new ArrayList<>(entries.keySet()).
